p.src: Now, just as Ping'er was laughing over what Yingchun had told her, Baoyu unexpectedly arrived as well. It turned out that the sister of Liu's wife, who managed the kitchens, had also got into trouble for running a gambling bank. Someone in the Garden who had long been on bad terms with the Liu family then denounced Mrs. Liu too, claiming that she and her sister were partners: although the sister acted as the figurehead, the two of them actually divided the profits equally. For this reason, Xifeng meant to punish Mrs. Liu. When Mrs. Liu heard the news, she panicked. Remembering that she had always been especially close to the people at Happy Red Court, she came secretly to beg Qingwen, Jinxing, Boli, and the others for help. Jinxing and Boli told Baoyu about it. Baoyu reflected that Yingchun's wet nurse was guilty of the same offense. It would therefore be more fitting to enlist Yingchun and plead for both of them than to go alone and intercede solely for Mrs. Liu; that was why he had come. Seeing so many people there, they all asked him when he entered, “Have you recovered from your illness? What have you come running here for?” Baoyu could hardly reveal that he had come to intercede, so he merely replied, “I've come to see Second Sister.” No one paid much attention to it, and they chatted idly for a while. Ping'er then went out to deal with the matter of the filigree gold phoenix. Wang Zhu'er's wife followed close behind, pleading in every possible way. “Please be merciful in what you say, miss. Whatever happens, I'll redeem it.” Ping'er laughed. “Whether sooner or later, you still have to redeem it. Since matters have come to this, why did you do it in the first place? You thought that if you could get away with it, the matter would simply be forgotten. Still, since you agree to this, I would feel awkward reporting you. Redeem it at once and give it to me to return, and I shall not say a single word about it.” Only then did Wang Zhu'er's wife feel relieved. She bowed her thanks and added, “Please go about your important business, miss. I shall bring it by this evening, report to you first, and then have it returned. Will that do?” Ping'er said, “If it isn't here by this evening, don't blame me for what happens.” After that, the two parted and went their separate ways. When Ping'er returned to the room, Xifeng asked her, “What did Third Miss want you for?” Ping'er smiled. “Third Miss was afraid you might be angry, madam, so she asked me to soothe you and inquire what you have been able to eat these past two days.” Xifeng laughed. “So she still remembers to care about me. Another affair came up just now: someone reported that Second Mrs. Liu and her sister had conspired to run a gambling house, and that everything her sister did was directed by her. I remembered how you are always urging me that ‘one less affair is better than one more,’ so that I might have a little peace and take better care of myself. Because I would not listen, just as you warned, I first offended Her Ladyship and then brought an illness upon myself into the bargain. Now I have seen through it all. Let them make whatever trouble they please; there are plenty of other people to deal with it. I wear myself out worrying, only to earn the curses of everyone around me.

p.src: Before she had finished speaking, Jia Lian entered, clapping his hands in vexation and sighing. “Now trouble has arisen again for no reason! How did Her Ladyship over there learn that I asked Yuanyang the other day to let me pawn some things? Just now she summoned me and ordered me to scrape together two hundred taels from somewhere or other for the Mid-Autumn Festival on the fifteenth day of the eighth month. I replied that I had nowhere to raise it. Then Her Ladyship said, ‘Whenever you need money, you can always find somewhere to raise it. I try to discuss the matter with you in good faith, but you merely put me off and claim there is nowhere to turn. Where did that thousand taels you raised by pawning things the other day come from? You were ingenious enough to get hold of even the Old Lady's belongings, yet now, when it is only two hundred taels, this is how you behave. Fortunately, I have not mentioned this to anyone else.’ It seems to me that Her Ladyship is clearly not short of money. Why must she pick a quarrel just to make things difficult for me?” Xifeng said, “There was not a single outsider present that day. Who could have leaked the news?” Hearing this, Ping'er carefully considered who had been present that day. After thinking for a long while, she smiled and said, “I know. There was no outsider there while we were talking, but when the things were delivered that evening, Silly Big Sister's mother from the Old Lady's quarters happened to come with some laundered clothes. She sat for a while in the servants' room and saw a large chest full of things, so naturally she would have asked about it. Perhaps the little maids, not realizing they should keep silent, told her.” They therefore summoned several young maids and asked which of them had told Silly Big Sister's mother about it that day. The young maids were terrified. They all knelt down, swearing solemn oaths. “We have never dared to say one word too many. Whenever anyone asks us anything, we always answer that we do not know. How could we possibly dare speak about such a matter?” After considering the matter, Xifeng said, “They certainly would not dare. We must not accuse them unjustly. Let us put that aside for now. The urgent thing is to satisfy Her Ladyship. Better for us to go short ourselves than invite another rebuff.” She then told Ping'er, “Bring me my gold neck-ring. Have it pawned for two hundred taels for the time being, send the money over, and settle the matter.” Jia Lian said, “Since we are doing it, we might as well pawn it for another two hundred. We need money ourselves.” Xifeng replied, “There is really no need. I have nowhere to spend money. Once it is pawned, who knows from which account we could ever find the money to redeem it?” Ping'er took the neck-ring and instructed someone to summon Wang'er's wife to collect it. Before long, the silver was brought back. Jia Lian personally delivered it, and nothing further need be said of the matter.

p.src: Before she had finished speaking, someone announced, “Her Ladyship is here.” Xifeng was startled to hear this. Wondering what could have brought her there in person, she hurried out with Ping'er and the others to meet her. Lady Wang approached with an even more altered countenance, attended by only one trusted young maid. Without saying a word, she went into the inner room and sat down. Xifeng hastened to offer her tea and asked with an ingratiating smile, “Are you in such fine spirits today, madam, that you have come here for a little visit?” Lady Wang barked an order: “Ping'er, get out!” Seeing her in this state, Ping'er grew alarmed and had no idea what had happened. She quickly answered, led all the young maids outside, and stopped beyond the doorway. She shut the door firmly, sat down on the stone step, and allowed no one at all to enter. Xifeng too became alarmed, not knowing what grave matter had occurred. Lady Wang, tears in her eyes, suddenly drew an embroidered pouch from her sleeve and flung it down. “Look at this,” she said. Xifeng hurriedly picked it up and examined it. Seeing that it was a many-colored erotic embroidered pouch, she too started in fright and asked, “Where did you get this, madam?” At this question Lady Wang's tears fell all the more heavily. In a trembling voice she said, “Where did I get it! I sit at the bottom of a well day after day, and because I took you for a careful and capable person, I allowed myself a little respite. Who would have thought that you were no better than I am? A thing like this was lying in broad daylight on a rock in the Garden and was picked up by one of the Old Lady's maids. Had your mother-in-law not happened upon her, it would long since have been taken straight to the Old Lady. Now tell me: how did this come to be left there?” Xifeng's expression changed still further when she heard this, and she hastily asked, “How do you know it is mine, madam?” Weeping and sighing, Lady Wang replied, “You have the nerve to question me! Think: apart from you young married couples, the rest of the household are old women. What use would they have for such a thing? And where could the unmarried girls have obtained it? Naturally that good-for-nothing, depraved Lian must have procured it somewhere. And the two of you have been getting along well. You took it for a plaything. Young married people may have their private intimacies in the bedchamber, but you still dare deny it to me! Fortunately, the servants throughout the Garden are still too innocent to understand such things, and none of them found it. But if one of the maids had picked it up and your young sisters had seen it, what a scandal that would have been! Or if one of the young maids had found it and gone out saying that she had picked it up in the Garden, and outsiders learned of it, would you have us lose both our lives and our good name?” Hearing this, Xifeng was both anxious and ashamed; her face instantly flushed a deep purple. She dropped to both knees beside the kang and, with tears in her eyes, pleaded, “What you say is certainly reasonable, madam, and I would not dare claim that I possess nothing of this sort. But I beg you to examine the matter closely: this pouch was embroidered by hired workers outside in imitation of the household's own needlework, and its cords and tassels are all ordinary wares sold in the market.

p.src: First, young and frivolous though I may be, I have no need of such a wretched thing; naturally, the relations between us are perfectly proper. Second, it is not something one carries about all the time. Even if I owned one, I would only keep it at home; why would I carry it everywhere on my person? Still less would I take it into the Garden, where we sisters are always playfully pulling one another about. If it happened to show, what face would I have—not merely before the sisters, but even if a servant saw it? Young and frivolous though I may be, I could not be so witless as that. Third, among the mistresses I may be a young daughter-in-law, but among the servants there is more than one woman younger than I am. They too often enter the Garden and return to their own quarters at night. How do we know it did not belong to one of them? Fourth, besides my frequent visits to the Garden, the lady from the other house often brings several young concubines there, such as Yanhong and Cuiyun. Being young women, they are still more likely to possess such a thing. Then there is Cousin Zhen's wife from that house, who can hardly be called old. She too often brings Peifeng and the others. How do we know it was not theirs? Fifth, there are so many maids in the Garden. Can anyone guarantee that every one of them is respectable? Some are old enough to know the ways of men and women. They may slip out when no one happens to be checking on them, or make some excuse to flirt and banter with the pageboys at the inner gate, and may have obtained it outside. Who can say? As matters stand, I can vouch not only for my own innocence but for Ping'er’s as well. Please consider all this carefully, madam.” Lady Wang found this argument entirely reasonable and sighed, “Get up. I know that you come from a great and respectable family. How could you be so wanton? I was merely beside myself with anger and used those words to provoke you. But what are we to do now? Your mother-in-law has just sent someone to bring me this, sealed up for my inspection. She said it was found in Silly Girl’s hands the day before yesterday. I was nearly beside myself with rage.” “Please do not be angry, madam,” said Xifeng. If everyone notices something is amiss, there is no telling but that the Old Lady will hear of it too. We should keep calm and investigate quietly before we can ascertain the truth. Even if we discover nothing, at least no outsider will learn of it. As the saying goes, ‘A broken arm must be kept inside the sleeve.’ Now that so many people have been dismissed on account of the gambling, we should seize the opportunity to place four or five close-mouthed, trustworthy women, such as Zhou Rui’s wife and Wang’er’s wife, inside the Garden on the pretext of investigating gambling. Besides, the young ladies now have far too many maids. With so many of them, some are bound to grow ambitious and cause mischief; once trouble breaks out, regret will come too late. Yet if we dismiss them now without cause, not only will the young ladies feel wronged and distressed, but you and I will find it hard to justify ourselves.

p.src: It would be better to take advantage of this opportunity: from now on, whenever one of the older maids, or some obstinate and troublesome one, commits a fault, we can drive her out and marry her off. That would both guard against further trouble and reduce expenses. What do you think of this proposal, madam?” Lady Wang sighed. “What you say is perfectly true, but if we consider the matter fairly and carefully, these sisters of yours are pitiable enough already. We need look no farther than the mother of your Cousin Lin. Before she married, how tenderly she was reared, how precious and honored she was! That was how a great family’s daughter ought to live. These sisters of yours nowadays live only slightly better than the maids in other households. Each has only two or three presentable maids in all; though there may be another four or five little girls, they are no better than the little demons in a temple. If we reduce their staffs still further, not only could I not bear it, but I fear the Old Lady would never consent. Times may be hard, but surely they have not come to this. Though I never enjoyed the greatest splendor and luxury, my upbringing was still better than yours. I would rather economize on myself now than let them suffer. If economies must be made in future, it would be better to begin with me. For now, summon Zhou Rui’s wife and the others, and instruct them to investigate the matter secretly and quickly. That is the urgent task.” On hearing this, Xifeng at once called Ping’er in and told her to convey the orders.

Lady Wang had just been worrying that there were too few people to conduct a proper search when Wang Shanbao’s wife, one of Lady Xing’s bondservants, came in; it was she who had brought the embroidered purse earlier. Lady Wang had always regarded Lady Xing’s trusted attendants without prejudice. Seeing now how earnestly Wang Shanbao’s wife had come to inquire about the matter, she said to her, “Go and report this to your mistress, then come into the garden and help supervise things. She had wanted to find some fault with them but never had the chance; this incident seemed to give her just the hold she needed. Lady Wang’s commission was exactly what she had hoped for, and she said, “That will be easy. Forgive this servant for speaking out of turn, but by rights stricter discipline should have been imposed long ago. Your Ladyship seldom goes into the garden, and those girls carry on as if each of them had received an imperial title. They behave as though they were highborn young ladies themselves. They could turn heaven upside down, and no one would dare utter a sound. Otherwise, they incite the young ladies’ maids to claim that their mistresses have been bullied—and who could bear the blame for that?” Lady Wang said, “That is only natural in a way. The maids who serve the young ladies are bound to be more indulged than the others. You ought to advise and correct them. Even the masters’ own daughters become impossible if they are not properly taught, let alone their maids.” Wang Shanbao’s wife replied, “The others are tolerable enough. She also has a clever tongue, dresses herself up every day like Xi Shi, and is glib, forward, and determined to outshine everyone. At the slightest word that displeases her, she rolls those wanton eyes and starts abusing people. With all her coquettish airs, she has no sense of propriety at all.” These words suddenly stirred an old memory in Lady Wang, and she asked Xifeng, “The last time we accompanied the Old Lady on a stroll through the garden, there was a girl with a slender waist and sloping shoulders, whose eyes and brows somewhat resembled your Cousin Lin’s. Later I meant to ask who she was, but happened to forget. Now that everything fits, I expect that girl must have been Qingwen.” Xifeng replied, “If all the maids are compared together, none is as pretty as Qingwen. As for her conduct and speech, she is indeed somewhat frivolous. The girl Your Ladyship just described does sound very much like her, but I too have forgotten what happened that day and dare not make a reckless claim.”

But when she reached Xifeng’s rooms, Lady Wang saw her hairpins askew and her tresses loose, her jacket hanging slack and her sash undone, bearing all the languorous charm of Xi Shi clasping her heart after waking in spring. Now that genuine anger had seized her and the former incident had returned to mind, she sneered, “What a beauty you are! You truly look like Xi Shi wasting away from illness. I shall leave you alone for now, but tomorrow I will certainly strip the hide from you! The Old Lady scolded me, saying, ‘No one is asking you to take charge of his affairs, so what need is there for cleverness?’ It was only after hearing that that I went. Once every ten days or a fortnight, if Baoyu feels bored, we all amuse ourselves together for a while and then disperse. p.src: At that time Li Wan was still ill in bed. Her quarters adjoined Xichun's and were also close to Tanchun's, so they stopped at those two places first along the way. Li Wan had only just fallen asleep after taking her medicine and could not be disturbed, so they merely searched the maids' rooms one by one. Finding nothing of consequence, they proceeded to Xichun's room. Since Xichun was young and knew little of worldly affairs, she was terrified, not knowing what might be happening, and Xifeng had no choice but to reassure her. To their surprise, however, they found in Ruhua's trunk a large packet containing some thirty or forty gold and silver ingots, as well as a set of jade belt plaques and a bundle of men's boots, socks, and other articles. Ruhua's face turned pale. When asked where the things had come from, Ruhua could only kneel down and tearfully confess the truth: “Master Zhen gave these to my elder brother. Our parents are both in the south, and now we live with our uncle. My uncle and aunt care for nothing but drinking and gambling. My brother feared that if he handed these things to them, they would spend them too, so whenever he received anything, he secretly asked an old nurse to bring it in for me to keep.” The timid Xichun was frightened by the sight of these things too. “I knew absolutely nothing about this,” she said. This is outrageous! Second Sister-in-law, if you mean to beat her, please take her outside and do it. I cannot bear to hear such things.” Xifeng laughed. “If her story is true, she may indeed be forgiven, except that the things should never have been smuggled in privately. If these things can be passed in, what could not be? The greater fault lies with the person who carried them in. But if this story is false and the things were stolen, you may give up all hope of living.” Still kneeling, Ruhua wept. “I would not dare tell a lie. Madam may ask our mistress and master tomorrow. If they say these things were not a reward, I will bear no grudge even if you beat my brother and me to death together.” “Naturally, we shall ask them,” said Xifeng. “But even if they truly were a reward, there is still wrongdoing here. Who gave you permission to pass things in privately? Just tell me who acted as your go-between, and I will pardon you. You must never do such a thing again.” Xichun said, “Sister-in-law, you must not pardon her this time. There are so many people here. Unless one person is made an example of, who knows what the older servants will do when they hear of it? If you pardon her, I shall not consent either.” Xifeng replied, “She has always seemed quite well behaved to me. Who has never made a mistake? We shall overlook it this once. If she offends a second time, she will be punished for both offenses. But I still do not know who carried the things in.” “If you mean the carrier, it could be no one else,” said Xichun. “It must have been Nanny Zhang at the back gate. She is forever behaving furtively with these maids, and they are always willing to oblige her.” On hearing this, Xifeng ordered the matter recorded and had the articles entrusted temporarily to Zhou Rui's wife, saying that they would verify everything and decide what to do the next day.

p.src: They then took leave of Xichun and went on to Yingchun's rooms. Yingchun was already asleep, and her maids were just preparing for bed. The party knocked for a long while before the door was opened. “There is no need to disturb the young lady,” Xifeng instructed them. She then proceeded to the maids' quarters. Since Siqi was the granddaughter of Wang Shanbao's wife, Xifeng was curious to see whether the woman would conceal anything belonging to her own family, and therefore watched her conduct the search with particular attention. They began by searching the others' trunks, but found nothing unusual. When they had searched Siqi's trunk for a while, Wang Shanbao's wife said, “There is nothing here either.” She was just about to close the lid when Zhou Rui's wife said, “Wait. What is this?” As she spoke, she reached in and pulled out a pair of men's brocade-banded socks and a pair of satin shoes. There was also a small bundle; when they opened it, they found inside a love-knot ruyi ornament and a written note. They handed all of it to Xifeng. Because Xifeng managed the household and frequently examined lists and accounts, she had learned to recognize a fair number of characters. She saw that the message was written on a bright-red sheet decorated with the double-happiness emblem. It read: “After you returned home last month, our parents became aware of the feelings between us. But while your young mistress remains unmarried, our own desire cannot yet be fulfilled. If there is any way for us to meet in the Garden, you may ask Nanny Zhang to send me word. If we could meet in the Garden, we would have a better chance to talk than when you come home. Please, I beg you. I have duly received the two scented sachets you sent me, and now I am sending you a string of fragrant beads as a small token of my affection. Be sure to keep it safe. Respectfully written by your cousin Pan You'an.” When Xifeng finished reading, instead of becoming angry, she was amused. None of the others could read. Wang Shanbao's wife had never known of this romantic affair between the cousins. The sight of the shoes and socks had already made her suspicious; then, seeing the red note and Xifeng smiling as she read it, she said, “They must have scribbled some muddled accounts that do not even resemble proper writing, and that is why Madam is laughing.” “Exactly,” Xifeng replied with a laugh. “This is indeed an account that simply will not balance. You are Siqi's grandmother, so her cousin ought to bear the surname Wang too. Why, then, is his surname Pan?” Wang Shanbao's wife found the question strange, but had no choice but to answer reluctantly, “Siqi's paternal aunt married into the Pan family, so her son, Siqi's cousin, bears the surname Pan. Pan You'an, the one who ran away last time, is that very cousin.” “That explains it,” said Xifeng with a laugh. Then she added, “I shall read it aloud for you.” With that, she read the note through from beginning to end, startling everyone. Wang Shanbao's wife had been intent only on finding fault with others, never imagining that she would instead catch her own granddaughter. She was furious and mortified. Zhou Rui's wife and the other three all asked her, “You heard that, did you not? It is perfectly clear, and there is nothing more to be said. Now, in your esteemed opinion, what ought to be done?”

p.src: Mrs. Wang wished the ground would open up and swallow her. Xifeng merely looked at her and giggled, then said laughingly to Mrs. Zhou, “This has turned out rather well. Without troubling either of you mothers in the least, she quietly found you an excellent son-in-law. That saves everyone a great deal of worry.” Mrs. Zhou joined in the laughter and added a few teasing remarks. With nowhere to vent her anger, Mrs. Wang turned her hand upon herself and slapped her own face, cursing, “You old whore who refuses to die—what sin have you brought upon yourself! My boasts have come back to slap me in the face; my punishment has overtaken me before everyone’s eyes.” At this spectacle, the others could not stop laughing, even as they half consoled and half mocked her. Xifeng saw that Siqi kept her head lowered without speaking, yet showed no sign of either fear or shame, and found this rather strange. Considering that it was already late at night, she decided there was no need to question her yet; but fearing that Siqi might take her own life in shame during the night, she ordered two old women to keep watch over her. She then took her people and the incriminating evidence back with her, retired for the night, and left the matter to be dealt with the following day. But during the night, unexpectedly, she had to get up several more times, and the bleeding below would not stop. By the next day she felt exceedingly weak; whenever she rose, her head swam, and at last she could no longer keep going. An imperial physician was summoned. After taking her pulse, he wrote his diagnosis: “The young mistress is suffering from insufficiency of the heart’s vital energy, with deficient fire invading the spleen. This has all been caused by anxiety and overwork, resulting in a constant desire to lie down and sleep; her stomach is depleted, the earth element is weak, and she has no appetite. For the present, I shall prescribe a remedy to raise the yang and nourish the vital energies.” Having written this, he prescribed several medicines, no more than such ingredients as ginseng, Chinese angelica, and astragalus. When the physician had gone, some of the old nurses took the prescription and reported to Lady Wang, adding yet another burden to her worries; consequently, the affair of Siqi and the others was left unattended for the time being.

p.src: As it happened, that day Madam You came to visit Xifeng. After sitting with her for a while, she went into the Garden and also called on Li Wan. Just as she was about to visit the other young ladies, a servant arrived with an invitation from Xichun, so Madam You went to her rooms. Xichun gave Madam You a detailed account of what had happened the previous night, then ordered that all of Ruhua’s belongings be brought for Madam You to inspect. Madam You said, “It is true that your brother gave these things to her brother. The only fault was that they were passed along privately, so now official salt has somehow become contraband salt.” She then scolded Ruhua for being “a muddleheaded fool whose wits were smothered in grease.” Xichun said, “You fail to discipline your people properly, yet you blame the maid. Of all the sisters, I alone have a maid who has brought such disgrace upon herself. How am I to face anyone? Yesterday I insisted that Sister Xifeng take her away, but she simply refused. Then I reflected that she originally came from your side, so Sister Xifeng had good reason not to take her. I was just going to send her back today, and your arrival, Sister-in-law, is most timely. Take her away at once. Whether you beat her, kill her, or sell her, I want nothing more to do with it.” Hearing this, Ruhua fell to her knees again and pleaded through her tears, “I shall never do it again. I beg you, miss, for the sake of all the years since I was little, let me remain with you in life or death.” Madam You, the nurse, and the others all argued earnestly on her behalf, saying, “She merely lost her wits for a moment and will never dare do it again. She has served you since childhood; surely it would be best to keep her.” But although Xichun was young, she was born with an unyielding, austere, solitary, and unsociable nature. No matter what anyone said, she believed her dignity had been compromised and, clenching her teeth, refused absolutely to relent. She went further, saying, “Not only do I refuse to keep Ruhua, but now that I am older, it is no longer proper for me to visit your side either. Besides, lately I have repeatedly heard rumors that people are discussing all manner of scandalous things behind your backs. If I continue going there, they will drag me into their stories as well.” Madam You asked, “Who has been saying what? And what is there to discuss? You are who you are, and we are who we are. Since you have heard people talking about us, you ought to question whoever said it.” Xichun gave a cold laugh. “It is curious that you should ask me that. As an unmarried girl, I should only keep away from scandal. If instead I went looking for trouble, what sort of person would that make me? There is one more thing: I am not afraid of angering you, but right and wrong will be judged by public opinion in any case, so why bother questioning anyone? The ancients put it well: ‘In good and evil, life and death, even father and son cannot help one another’—much less you and I. All I know is that it is enough for me to preserve myself; I shall not concern myself with any of you. From now on, whatever happens on your side, do not involve me.” Hearing this, Madam You was both angry and amused. Turning to the people standing below, she said, “No wonder everyone says that Fourth Miss is young and foolish. I was the only one who would not believe it.

I beg you, miss, for the sake of all the years since I was little, let me remain with you in life or death.”
Madam You, the nurse, and the others all argued earnestly on her behalf, saying, “She merely lost her wits for a moment and will never dare do it again.
She has served you since childhood; surely it would be best to keep her.”

But although Xichun was young, she was born with an unyielding, austere, solitary, and unsociable nature. No matter what anyone said, she believed her dignity had been compromised and, clenching her teeth, refused absolutely to relent.
She went further, saying, “Not only do I refuse to keep Ruhua, but now that I am older, it is no longer proper for me to visit your side either.
Besides, lately I have repeatedly heard rumors that people are discussing all manner of scandalous things behind your backs. If I continue going there, they will drag me into their stories as well.”
Madam You asked, “Who has been saying what?
And what is there to discuss?
You are who you are, and we are who we are.
Since you have heard people talking about us, you ought to question whoever said it.”
Xichun gave a cold laugh. “It is curious that you should ask me that.
As an unmarried girl, I should only keep away from scandal. If instead I went looking for trouble, what sort of person would that make me?
There is one more thing: I am not afraid of angering you, but right and wrong will be judged by public opinion in any case, so why bother questioning anyone?
The ancients put it well: ‘In good and evil, life and death, even father and son cannot help one another’—much less you and I.
All I know is that it is enough for me to preserve myself; I shall not concern myself with any of you.
From now on, whatever happens on your side, do not involve me.”

Hearing this, Madam You was both angry and amused. Turning to the people standing below, she said, “No wonder everyone says that Fourth Miss is young and foolish. I was the only one who would not believe it.
